content.user_title: Extract Brand Colors from CSS Variables
content.value_statement: Finding brand colors manually in website CSS takes time. This guide helps an AI agent generate reusable Python extraction scripts focused on brand CSS variables.
actual_capabilities: Guides an AI agent to generate a standalone Python script for extracting color values from public website CSS variables.
Identifies primary, accent, and brand variable naming conventions as extraction targets.
Specifies Python standard-library implementation without third-party dependencies.
Provides a sample request and describes the intended generated script.
Documents extraction boundaries for JavaScript, shadow DOM, images, and computed styles.
limitations: Only SKILL.md is included; the referenced scripts, extension source, and templates are not bundled.
Extraction targets CSS variables, not images, logos, rendered pixels, or computed styles.
The guide excludes colors set through JavaScript, hidden shadow DOM content, and pages requiring login.
Generated scripts are not provided or tested here; results depend on agent implementation and website structure.

prompt_templates.title: Start with One Website
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a Python script to extract primary, accent, and brand color hex values from CSS variables at [public URL].
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: create an initial extraction script.

prompt_templates.title: Focus on Brand Tokens
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a standard-library Python script for [public URL]. Filter CSS variables for primary, accent, and brand names, retaining each variable name.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: narrow the results to meaningful brand tokens.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Two Pages
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a reusable Python extraction script for [URL A] and [URL B]. Compare matching brand CSS variable names and report differing hex values.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: request a comparison workflow based on the extraction guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Specify a Robust Extraction Script
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a standard-library Python extractor for [public URL]. Include request timeouts, explicit failures, duplicate handling, and source labels. State unsupported CSS cases.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: specify implementation safeguards and output requirements.

output_examples.input: Summarize candidate colors when supplied CSS defines --primary as #1258A8 and --accent as #F2C94C.
output: These values come from the supplied CSS, not a live website scan.

output_examples.input: Explain the result when the retrieved CSS contains no matching brand variables.
output: No matching primary, accent, or brand CSS variables were found in the retrieved content.
This does not establish that the website has no brand colors.
JavaScript colors, images, and computed styles are outside the documented scope.

best_practices: Use public websites you are authorized to inspect and review generated scripts before execution.
Keep CSS variable names alongside hex values so designers can verify intended color roles.
Check extracted values against the source CSS and document unsupported or missing content.
anti_patterns: Assuming the package already includes a working Python extractor.
Treating every matching variable as an authoritative brand color without verification.
Expecting CSS variable extraction to recover colors from logos, JavaScript, or login-protected pages.

faq.question: Is a ready-to-run extractor included?
faq.answer: No. This package contains only SKILL.md and asks an AI agent to generate the extraction script.

faq.question: Which color definitions does the guide target?
faq.answer: It targets CSS custom properties with names such as --primary, --accent, and --brand.

faq.question: Does the generated script require third-party libraries?
faq.answer: The guide specifies Python standard libraries only. Review the generated script to confirm it follows that requirement.

faq.question: Can it extract colors from images or rendered pages?
faq.answer: No. Image processing, rendered pixels, computed styles, JavaScript-defined colors, and hidden shadow DOM content are outside the documented scope.

faq.question: Can I use this guide with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: These agents can use the guide to generate code. Running the generated script requires Python and network access to the target website.

faq.question: Does a missing result mean the website has no brand colors?
faq.answer: No. Colors may use different variable names or appear in content the generated script does not retrieve or support.
